totals.rows_scoped: instructions, contract.invariants, contract.not_exposed, best_practices across the 11 cap-layer implement facets named in the task (cap-agent-runtime-implement, cap-capability-packaging-implement, cap-capability-registry-implement, cap-document-validation-implement, cap-durable-execution-implement, cap-errors-implement, cap-evaluation-implement, cap-human-interaction-implement, cap-idempotency-implement, cap-identity-implement, cap-isolation-implement). contract.shapes, definition_of_done, adapters and composes_with were off limits per instruction and not touched.

method: For every proposed row, checked whether it (a) restated its ideal cap-* sibling's own contract or another skill in this ceremony's scope, (b) rewrote another row already present in the same skill file (most often the differs_in_execution_model axes already spelled out in that skill's own adapters.swap_procedure fields, which are off limits to edit but readable), (c) was generic engineering advice with no capability-specific content, or (d) carried a specific, sourceable claim. Category (a)/(b) rows were shrunk to a one-clause pointer naming the sibling or the adapters section (kept origin=proposed, since a pointer is structure, not a citation); this fired for the near-identical differs_in_execution_model invariant repeated across cap-agent-runtime-implement, cap-durable-execution-implement and cap-isolation-implement, for the near-identical 'honest declared gap, no emulation' best-practice repeated across the same three skills plus a cap-agent-runtime-implement-only instance, for the binding-record-shape invariant repeated near-verbatim across cap-capability-packaging-implement, cap-capability-registry-implement and cap-document-validation-implement, for each of those three skills' not_exposed row (which already restated their ideal sibling's own sourced not_exposed row about transport/storage-layout/adapter-error exclusions), and for one each in cap-idempotency-implement and cap-identity-implement whose invariant restated their own ideal sibling's already-sourced idempotency-conflict / identity-untrusted failure-type row. Category (c) was deleted outright: cap-capability-packaging-implement and cap-capability-registry-implement each carried a best_practices row asserting 'a typed resolution failure, not a crash at start-up' that added nothing capability-specific beyond generic reliability advice already covered by cap-errors' typed-failure contract; both were removed rather than converted or pointered, since neither is this facet's own design. Category (d) rows were converted to origin=sourced only when a verbatim quote from a cited kb record supported the row's own specific claim, not merely its vocabulary: the single largest source of conversions was the repeated 'X states design rule N (F-id); what this adds is Z' shape already used correctly by already-sourced rows in the same 11 skills, applied to F-b1-02 (core imports interfaces), F-b1-04 (second adapter proves the first is not load-bearing), F-a7-02 (correlation rides on an explicit resource attribute), F-a7-04 (configuration written in the documented place had no runtime effect), F-b3-16/F-b2-06 (idempotency-key-on-the-wire and Ledger-is-the-deduplication-authority), F-a6-06 (typed errors absent), and T-t2-03 (every cross-cutting concern managed across the entire structure whichever entry point was used) - concentrated in cap-idempotency-implement and cap-identity-implement, whose TARGET T2.3 placement instructions and correlation-wiring instructions had carried real citations while still marked proposed. A handful of rows (cap-document-validation-implement's 'run both adapters over the platform's own instances', cap-isolation-implement's configuration-swap invariant) converted on a single research.jsonl or fact record whose snippet literally contained the claim. Rows with only an adjacent or thematically-similar record (cap-idempotency-implement's canonical-bytes-digest invariant on X-cap-idempotency-002, cap-identity-implement's delegate-unsupported invariant on X-cross-structure-034, its credentials-never-reach-the-log invariant on X-cross-structure-006, cap-durable-execution-implement's migration-order instruction on T-t6-01) were left proposed rather than force-converted, since the cited record's own text does not state the row's specific claim. The remaining 69 proposed rows had a 'Research query:' sentence appended to their text (or their instruction's 'why' field) naming the specific record, measurement or migration precedent that would source them; the two references/*.md progressive-disclosure pointer rows already present per skill (14 total across the 11 skills, one per -implement facet plus one duplicate in a couple) and the already-established 'Apply build-adapter-pair/build-definition-of-done/build-evidence-record: ...; proposed pointer, see that skill' rows were left untouched with no added query, matching the sourcing-01/02a/02b precedent that a navigational or already-correctly-formatted pointer row is not researchable in the same sense.
quality_note: Every candidate quote was checked programmatically as a literal substring of at least one of its row's cited kb records before conversion, including the json.dumps fallback validate_skills.py itself uses for research.jsonl records with no text field (X-cap-idempotency-007, X-cap-idempotency-006, X-cap-identity-004, X-cap-document-validation-006). Every skill was rendered with tools/render_skill.py and checked with tools/validate_skills.py --only <skill> after every edit; a pre-ceremony baseline warning count and content was captured for each of the 11 skills before any row was touched (git stash / git show HEAD), and the post-ceremony run for each skill was diffed against that baseline line by line, not just by count. Several conversions initially introduced a new 'restates F-id/X-id under the same quote as <sibling>, without naming it (compose by name, not by copy)' warning because the newly-sourced row's quote collided with an already-sourced row elsewhere in the same skill or in a builds_on sibling (cap-errors-implement on F-meta-04 against build-adapter-pair and on X-cap-errors-005 against cap-errors' own best_practices; cap-idempotency-implement on F-b2-06 against cap-idempotency and on T-t2-03 against build-definition-of-done, the last reused across three converted rows in that one skill; cap-identity-implement on F-a7-02 against cap-identity; cap-human-interaction-implement on F-a7-04 against build-evidence-record) - each was resolved by naming the colliding owner in the row's own text (never by leaving the collision, per the compose-by-name rule) and re-validated until the warning was gone rather than merely moved. A second class of new warning came from converting a row whose text used the 'already states'/'what X adds' phrasing without the schema's required 'proposed' marker inside a now-origin=sourced row (MECH-2, tools/validate_skills.py RESTATE_MARKER); every such row was reworded to drop the trigger phrase rather than kept and accepted as a new warning. Final result for all 11 skills: 0 errors, and every skill's own --only warning count and content is byte-identical to its pre-ceremony baseline (cap-agent-runtime-implement 5, cap-capability-packaging-implement 1, cap-capability-registry-implement 2, cap-document-validation-implement 9, cap-durable-execution-implement 7, cap-errors-implement 6, cap-evaluation-implement 0, cap-human-interaction-implement 1, cap-idempotency-implement 0, cap-identity-implement 0, cap-isolation-implement 8) - no new restatement warning survived under any of the 11 skills' own name. adapters, definition_of_done, contract.shapes and composes_with were not read for editing purposes beyond using their existing text (adapters.swap_procedure, mainly) to confirm a within-skill duplication before shrinking a row to a pointer; none of those four sections was modified.
